newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Frenchman takes over U.N. Guatemalan operation.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman takes over U.N. Guatemalan operation.

text.p: Jean Arnault of France, who served as mediator for the Guatemalan peace accords, will take over as civilian head of U.N. operations in the Central American country, a U.N. spokesman announced on Monday.
He replaces David Stephen of Britain and will be special representative for the U.N. Vertification Mission in Guatemala, spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said.
Stephen, a former speechwriter in the secretary-general's oflfice who went to Guatemala only seven months go, will become chief speechwriter under Secretary-General Kofi Annan, U.N. officials said.

The operation involves a 500-strong human rights monitoring mission along with the recently-approved 155 military observers to help implement the recent peace accords that ended 36 years of civil war.

Under the Dec. 29 peace agreements, the Guatemalan army is to cut its numbers and about 3,000 guerrillas from the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) are to go to assembly points, disarm and be integrated into civilian life. U.N. observers will monitor assembly points.
Brandt on Friday announced that Brig. Gen. Jose B. Rodriguez of Spain would head the peacekeeping contingent.
